core.text: Candidate A: refresh, then inspect/select the explicit key, then commit without an intervening refresh. Repeat for K2, K5, K7 during minutes 0-3, 3-6, 6-9. Refreshes complete at 1, 4, 7; the last loads S2. The stipulated model predicts correct writes because loaded row order stays fixed between each selection and commit. Nine-minute feasibility is prospective; log every actual key.

Candidate B: use the available immutable-key binding control. Inspect/select, refresh, commit for each target in three consecutive three-minute blocks. Refreshes complete at 2, 5, 8, so final S2 is loaded. The hypothesis predicts K2, K5, K7 writes despite reordering. This evaluates a supported synthetic control; it does not establish that a production editor offers key binding.

Candidate C: retain S0 for inspect/select-and-commit pairs during minutes 0-2, 2-4, 4-6, then refresh during 6-7. Predicted writes follow S0 rows 2, 5, 7; the final refresh loads S2 while preserving statuses by key. Seven minutes and one refresh are modeled estimates pending replay. Compare this with the nine-minute alternatives against the same unchanged success criteria.

residue.text: Verification proposal: replay each candidate independently from all-unchecked S0. Record times, snapshots, selected rows, intended keys and every actual write. Require exactly K2/K5/K7 checked, all other statuses unchecked, unchanged source scores, no incorrect-key write even if repaired, latest snapshot loaded and completion within ten minutes.

The supplied evidence establishes one synthetic miswrite, not successful completion or recurring mismatch feedback. Equal scores for K5 and K7 require key-based checking. Real binding, detection costs and failures remain unknown; connectors and participants are absent. Any recurrence mechanism or practical benefit remains a hypothesis.
